name: Mellah
hero_subtitle: The historic Jewish quarter woven into Essaouira’s medina — quieter lanes and a layered past.

overview.title: A quarter of memory
overview.p1: Essaouira’s Mellah is the historic Jewish neighbourhood within the wider medina. Streets are often quieter than the main tourist arteries; the interest is atmosphere and urban history more than monuments.
overview.p2: Walk respectfully, be discreet with photos around homes, and treat the Mellah as part of a broader medina loop rather than a long stop on its own.
overview.p3: Pair it with the Skala and the artisan souks for a full reading of the town’s communities and trade.

food.title: Food near the Mellah

1.title: Access
1.desc: Reached on foot inside the medina; ask if you leave the main lanes.

2.title: Respect
2.desc: Discreet photography — this remains a lived-in neighbourhood.

3.title: Time
3.desc: Forty-five to ninety minutes within a wider medina walk is enough.

q1.question: Is there a ticket?
q1.answer: No. It is a living neighbourhood of streets to walk.

q2.question: Guided tours?
q2.answer: Local guides can add names and stories if you want deeper context.

q3.question: How long?
q3.answer: About an hour within a wider medina walk.

q4.question: Safe?
q4.answer: Daytime is usual; stay on busier lanes if unsure.

q5.question: Combine with the souks?
q5.answer: Yes — Mellah and craft streets sit in the same medina fabric.
